title: Torque Specification — M8 Bolts on Assembly Jig A3
steps: Ensure the bolt threads are clean and free of debris before torquing.
Select a calibrated torque wrench rated for the target range (20–25 Nm).
Apply a thin layer of anti-seize compound to the bolt threads.
Hand-tighten the bolt until snug, confirming the washer is seated.
Set the torque wrench to 22 Nm and apply torque in a smooth, continuous motion.
Mark the bolt head with a paint marker to confirm torque completion.
Record the torque value and operator ID in the assembly checklist (Form MFG-A3-012).

title: Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) — CNC Milling Machine LM-400
steps: Notify all affected employees before initiating LOTO on LM-400.
Power down the machine using the main control panel — confirm display goes dark.
Turn the main disconnect switch to the OFF position at the electrical panel.
Apply your personal lock to the hasp on the disconnect — only you hold the key.
Attach a LOTO tag with your name, employee ID, date, and reason for lockout.
Release stored energy: bleed any residual pneumatic pressure via the relief valve.
Attempt to restart the machine from the control panel to verify zero energy state.
Proceed with maintenance only after zero energy is confirmed.

title: Visual Inspection Criteria — Weld Quality on Frame Sub-Assembly
steps: Allow weld to cool to ambient temperature before inspection.
Use a 5× magnifying glass and adequate lighting (min 500 lux) at the inspection station.
Check for surface porosity — any pore diameter > 1.5 mm is a rejection criterion.
Inspect for undercut along the weld toe — depth > 0.5 mm requires rework.
Measure weld leg length with a weld gauge — minimum 6 mm on all fillet welds.
Check for cracks, spatters > 3 mm, and overlap defects at start/stop points.
Mark non-conforming welds with red chalk and tag the part with a red NCR tag.
Complete Weld Inspection Form QA-WLD-07 and forward to the Quality Engineer.

title: Machine Error Code Response — Error E-14 (Spindle Overload)
steps: Do not attempt to clear E-14 without investigating root cause first.
Press the FEED HOLD button immediately to stop axis movement safely.
Record the active alarm code and current spindle load percentage from the HMI.
Check the cutting tool for wear or breakage — replace if flute damage is visible.
Verify the programmed feed rate and spindle speed against the approved NC program.
Reduce feed-rate override to 70% and attempt a trial cut on scrap material.
If overload recurs, inspect the spindle motor cooling fan for blockage.
If the fault persists after corrective action, raise a Work Order for maintenance.

title: PPE Requirements — Plasma Cutting Operations
steps: Wear a welding helmet with shade 5 or higher filter lens for plasma arc exposure.
Don flame-resistant (FR) overalls rated to EN ISO 11611 — no synthetic fibres.
Use leather welding gloves — minimum 30 cm cuff length to protect forearms.
Wear steel-toe leather safety boots with metatarsal protection.
Ensure respiratory protection (FFP2 minimum) is worn when cutting galvanised steel.
Use hearing protection (SNR ≥ 25 dB) if ambient noise exceeds 85 dB(A).
Confirm a Class D fire extinguisher is within reach before starting the operation.
Inspect all PPE for damage before use; damaged items must not be worn.

title: Torque Specification — M12 Bolts on Gearbox Cover
steps: Degrease mating surfaces with isopropyl alcohol and allow to fully dry.
Apply a thread-locking compound (Loctite 243) to the M12 bolt threads.
Hand-start all bolts in the gearbox cover before applying any torque.
Follow a cross-pattern tightening sequence to ensure even gasket compression.
Torque to 40 Nm in two passes: first 20 Nm, then final 40 Nm.
Allow thread-locking compound to cure for 30 minutes before pressure testing.
Log torque values, operator ID, and curing start time on the Gearbox Assembly Record.

title: Visual Inspection Criteria — Surface Finish on Machined Aluminium Parts
steps: Clean the part with compressed air and a lint-free cloth before inspection.
Measure surface roughness with a calibrated profilometer — reject if Ra > 1.6 µm on sealing faces.
Inspect for burrs at all drilled holes and machined edges using a 10× loupe.
Deburr any burr height > 0.1 mm using a deburring tool before re-inspection.
Check dimensional tolerances against the drawing for critical features.
Inspect for tool marks, chatter marks, or gouges — any visible chatter is a re-machine trigger.
Record pass/fail status on the In-Process Inspection Record (QA-MFG-IP-04).

title: Machine Error Code Response — Error E-07 (Axis Servo Fault)
steps: Immediately initiate an E-stop to prevent any further uncontrolled axis movement.
Note which axis (X, Y, or Z) triggered the servo fault from the alarm log.
Power cycle the machine controller after waiting 60 seconds for capacitors to discharge.
If the fault clears on restart, perform a slow jog on the affected axis to check smooth movement.
Inspect the servo drive LED status codes — red solid indicates hardware failure.
Check cable connections at the servo drive and the axis motor terminal box.
If the fault persists, contact the OEM service line and log in the Maintenance Register.

title: Defect Classification — Injection-Moulded Plastic Parts
steps: Inspect the part under 500 lux uniform lighting against a neutral grey background.
Identify sink marks: depressions visible as shadows on A-surfaces are critical defects.
Check for flash along parting lines — flash > 0.5 mm extending into a functional zone is a reject.
Inspect weld lines on visible surfaces — any weld line breaking the surface colour uniformity is a reject.
Measure short-shot depth with a depth gauge — any short > 0.3 mm is an immediate reject.
Identify burn marks (dark discolouration at gate or end-of-fill areas) — always reject.
Record each defect type, location, and quantity on the Injection Moulding NCR Form (QA-IM-03).
Segregate rejected parts in a red-labelled quarantine bin.

title: Lockout/Tagout — Hydraulic Press HP-200
steps: Inform the press operator and adjacent workstation operators before applying LOTO.
Lower the ram to the bottom dead-centre position to minimise stored energy.
Shut off the hydraulic power unit and wait for the pressure gauge to read zero.
Isolate the electrical supply at the MCC panel and apply a personal lock.
Bleed residual hydraulic pressure via the manual pressure-relief valve.
Block the ram mechanically using the approved safety block before working under it.
Verify zero energy state: attempt to initiate a press cycle from the pendant — nothing should move.
Attach a LOTO tag with name, date, and reason, visible from the operator position.

title: Torque Specification — Cylinder Head Bolts (Engine Sub-Assembly)
steps: Verify that all mating surfaces are clean and the head gasket is correctly oriented.
Lubricate bolt threads and washer faces with fresh engine oil — do not reuse old bolts.
Install bolts finger-tight in the manufacturer's specified sequence.
Apply first torque pass: 30 Nm in sequence.
Apply second torque pass: 60 Nm in sequence.
Apply third torque pass: 90 Nm in sequence.
Apply final angular torque: +90° rotation per bolt in sequence using an angle gauge.
Mark all bolt heads with a stripe using a paint marker to confirm completion.
Record all torque values and lot numbers in the Engine Build Record.

title: PPE Requirements — Chemical Cleaning Station
steps: Review the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for the specific cleaning agent before starting.
Wear nitrile chemical-resistant gloves rated to EN 374 — minimum 0.4 mm thickness.
Don a full-face shield (not safety glasses) when handling solvents above 100 ml.
Wear an organic vapour respirator (EN 14387 A1) in enclosed or poorly ventilated spaces.
Use a rubber apron over FR overalls to protect against splashes.
Ensure eyewash station is within 10 seconds' reach before beginning any chemical work.
Never eat, drink, or touch your face while working with chemical cleaning agents.
Dispose of contaminated cleaning cloths in the designated yellow chemical-waste bin.

title: Machine Error Code Response — Error E-22 (Coolant Pressure Low)
steps: Stop the current machining operation and set the spindle to zero rpm.
Check the coolant tank level — minimum level is marked at the 10-litre line.
If tank is low, top up with approved water-soluble coolant to the 15-litre mark.
Inspect the coolant pump filter for swarf blockage — clean with a plastic brush.
Check the coolant delivery hose for kinks or disconnections at the nozzle.
Verify coolant pressure at the pressure gauge after pump restart — target 3.5–4.5 bar.
If pressure remains low after all checks, contact maintenance to inspect the pump impeller.
Log the event and corrective action in the Machine Maintenance Log (Form MNT-CNC-01).

title: Visual Inspection — Painted Exterior Panels (Class A Surface)
steps: Inspect the panel under a 60-degree incidence light source in a dedicated paint-inspection booth.
Check for orange peel texture — use a BYK Wave-Scan instrument; DOI < 85 is a reject.
Inspect for runs or sags — any run thicker than 0.3 mm in a visible zone is a reject.
Check for dirt inclusions using a 5× loupe — inclusions > 0.5 mm are a reject.
Look for colour mismatch against the approved master panel at normal viewing distance (1 m).
Measure film thickness with a dry-film gauge — specified range 90–130 µm.
Any defect on a Class A (visible) surface triggers an immediate repair-or-reject decision.
Document findings on the Paint Inspection Report and attach to the job traveller.

title: Defect Classification — Electrical PCB Visual Inspection
steps: Inspect the PCB under 10× magnification with oblique lighting to highlight solder surfaces.
Identify cold solder joints: dull, grainy, or rough surfaces indicate inadequate reflow.
Check for solder bridges between adjacent pads — any bridge is an immediate reject.
Inspect component orientation against the Bill of Materials and assembly drawing.
Verify all through-hole components are fully seated — 0.5 mm gap between body and board is acceptable max.
Check pad lifting or delamination with a 0.1 mm feeler gauge at suspect areas.
Identify missing components by comparing to the BOM line-by-line.
Log all defects on the PCB Inspection Record and route non-conforming boards to rework.

title: Conveyor Belt Safety Inspection — Weekly Check
steps: Isolate the conveyor under LOTO before any physical inspection of moving parts.
Visually inspect the belt surface for cuts, fraying, or delamination — 50 mm belt width loss is a replacement trigger.
Check belt tracking — belt edge must not contact the frame; adjust tracking rollers if drift exceeds 10 mm.
Measure belt tension with a tension meter — refer to belt specification sheet for target tension.
Inspect all idler rollers for bearing noise and smooth rotation by hand.
Check drive pulley lagging for wear — worn lagging exceeding 30% of surface area must be replaced.
Inspect emergency pull-cord switches along the conveyor length — verify each actuates an E-stop.
Complete the Weekly Conveyor Inspection Checklist (SAFE-CONV-WK) and submit to the Safety Officer.

title: Dimensional Inspection — First Article Inspection (FAI) Protocol
steps: Confirm part number and revision match the approved drawing before measuring.
Conduct all dimensional measurements on a temperature-stabilised CMM at 20 ± 2 °C.
Measure all critical dimensions (annotated 'K' on the drawing) first.
Record each measurement against the nominal value and tolerance band in the FAI report.
Any out-of-tolerance critical dimension stops production — do not continue to secondary operations.
Measure GD&T features using the appropriate datum structure as defined on the drawing.
Photograph any non-conforming feature and attach to the FAI report.
Submit the completed FAI package to Quality Assurance for sign-off before series production release.

title: Forklift Pre-Use Inspection Checklist
steps: Check the operator licence card is present and valid before use.
Inspect the fork tines for cracks, bends, or wear — blade thickness reduction > 10% is a withdrawal criterion.
Check tyre condition and inflation pressure (pneumatic) or wear (solid); bald tyres must not be used.
Test all lights: head, tail, and strobe must be operational.
Test the horn — audible from 5 m minimum.
Check hydraulic fluid level in the reservoir; top up with approved fluid if below the MIN mark.
Test lift and tilt functions through full range under no load.
Confirm the battery charge level (electric) or fuel level (propane/diesel) is adequate for the shift.
Record the inspection results on the Forklift Daily Pre-Use Checklist (LOG-FLT-01).

title: Rework Procedure — Paint Defect Spot Repair
steps: Identify and mark the defect boundaries with a wax pencil — include a 50 mm feathering zone.
Sand the defect area with P400 wet-and-dry paper, then P800, keeping the surface wet.
Blow dry with compressed air and solvent wipe the repair zone with a tack cloth.
Apply a primer coat and allow to flash off for 15 minutes at 20 °C.
Apply the topcoat in two medium-wet coats with a 5-minute flash-off between coats.
Bake the repair at 60 °C for 30 minutes in the touch-up oven.
After cooling, wet-sand with P1500 paper, then machine-polish with a DA polisher.
Inspect the repaired area against the master panel in the inspection booth before approving.

title: PPE Requirements — Grinding and Deburring Operations
steps: Wear a full-face shield over safety glasses — sparks and fragments can travel up to 3 m.
Use cut-resistant gloves rated EN 388 level 4 — leather welding gloves are also acceptable.
Don FR coveralls — no exposed cotton or synthetic clothing.
Wear hearing protection (SNR ≥ 27 dB) — bench grinders exceed 100 dB(A) at operator position.
Ensure steel-toe and steel-midsole safety boots are worn.
Inspect the grinding disc before fitting — any crack, chip, or damage means discard and replace.
Check wheel guard is in place and positioned correctly before starting the grinder.
Never grind in the direction of other personnel; ensure a 3 m exclusion zone is maintained.
